Name: Planning Overhaul
Description:
[h2]Planning Overhaul[/h2]

Ever designed an entire ship with the Planning tool, started construction, and discovered that the plan had no opinion about rooms, material limits, or the Ship Computer sitting under tomorrow's new floor? Well, have I got an aggressively organized construction schedule for you!

Planning Overhaul turns the vanilla Planning overlay into a layered ship-design system. Draw complete rooms with real buildings, reserve staging areas, and let Pulse Wave or Continuous construction carry the design through Core's normal jobs.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]Layered Construction Planning[/h3]
- Plans floors, walls, doors, and equipment together without flattening them into one visible layer
- Keeps saved ghosts visible while the active preview moves across the map
- Draws complete multi-tile building images with a lighter footprint in the active Planning color
- Uses last placement wins within each layer, so a wall line can be drawn before its doors
- Provides a Plan Eraser that removes the highest plan layer while preserving lower layers and staging
- Applies 384 Paint-style planning colors by room or building type without painting constructed tiles

[h3]Rooms and Building Catalog[/h3]
- Organizes Core and compatible modded buildings by their native translated categories and order
- Adds named, color-keyed rooms with center-focused selection and visible map labels
- Orders captured or imported interior rooms from the center outward and keeps Exterior last
- Keeps large catalogs, room sequences, and saved-blueprint lists inside bounded controls
- Allows one room or the complete plan to be reset while completed buildings remain intact

[h3]Pulse Wave and Continuous Construction[/h3]
- Queues construction and replacement through normal Stardeus jobs
- Runs enclosed rooms through structure, clearing, power, atmosphere, and equipment
- Gives Exterior a connected-floor policy, then admits every other building when its local floor is ready
- Yields rooms blocked by research, active work, materials, relocation, staging, or disconnected floors so later rooms can progress
- Advances floors only from cardinally adjacent completed floors and never queues floating tiles
- Restores missing native structural jobs and periodically rechecks deferred rooms
- Finishes with production, Transporter, upgrade, and planter configuration passes
- Disables itself after every planned room and retained setting matches

[h3]Materials, Staging, and Reuse[/h3]
- Requires normal construction cost plus a 10% per-material stock buffer
- Queues the affordable part of large stages while retaining one live material budget
- Publishes ordinary Lacking materials requests when the optional Auto Factory mod is present
- Adds Indoor, Outdoor, and Outdoor Edge staging with appropriate clearance rules
- Uses native priority-5 relocation jobs and moves compatible buildings directly to final destinations before staging
- Batches ready final moves against half the living crew while keeping staging admission one move at a time
- Reuses displaced walls and equipment before constructing replacement copies
- Treats required input and interaction cells as functional clearance when finding blockers
- Requires a powered destination connector before relocating configured production buildings

[h3]Optional Construction Support[/h3]
- Prioritizes blueprint Nanobot Hives and runtime-detected Quantum Storage endpoints after connected power
- Adds a missing Hive and raw-material Quantum Storage Unit only when definitions, research, safe floor space, materials, and power permit
- Extends optional support across large Exterior frontiers without occupying planned building footprints
- Keeps support non-blocking, outside exported blueprint entries, and dependency-free when Quantum Storage is absent

[h3]Reusable Blueprints and Configuration[/h3]
- Captures constructed ships into named rooms, layered entries, and staging areas
- Saves blueprints locally or copies the active plan as a shareable code
- Preserves centered coordinates across map sizes and rejects actual content that cannot fit
- Retains ordinary production queues, Transporter names and links, installed upgrades, and planter settings
- Leaves Nano Fabricator, Nano Foundry, and Nano Cloning Pod queues under Auto Factory control when that mod is loaded
- Provides separate load, delete, import, capture, and confirmed full-plan clear controls

[h3]Upgrades and Status[/h3]
- Creates Core-compatible replacement tasks for selected floors, walls, and doors
- Reports active jobs, workers, priorities, shortages, blocked coordinates, and placement reasons
- Keeps paused inspection tied to the room selected by the player
- Updates live construction details without repeatedly rebuilding the complete panel

[h2]Safety and Player Control[/h2]

Planning Overhaul creates normal construction, replacement, relocation, deconstruction, configuration, and upgrade work. Core retains material hauling, worker selection, reachability, task execution, and completion behavior. Correctly placed buildings remain in place.

Ship Computer and Quantum Ship Computer buildings are never selected for planner-driven demolition or destructive replacement. They may move through Core's relocation system when they block construction, but wait for a suitable destination. Sandbox floor replacement also waits until supported equipment or walls can move safely.

Stasis Array, Particle Collector, Core chess pieces, and Mysterious Statue are protected originals. The planner may relocate them to compatible destinations, but does not construct replacement copies or order their demolition. Player-issued native work remains under player control.

[h2]Performance[/h2]

Large plans use indexed room, definition, footprint, and occupancy data with bounded construction batches. Exterior reuses a short-lived active-work candidate cache instead of rebuilding the complete plan state every automation pass. Current satisfaction, floor readiness, placement, relocation capacity, and Core authority are checked before each order.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]

Requires [b]Stardeus 0.15.0[/b] and [b]Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0[/b]. AUMF supplies the managed Planning window and compatibility handshake. Its DLL remains a separate dependency and is not bundled.

[h2]In Short[/h2]

You draw the rooms and choose the buildings. Stardeus supplies the materials and workers. Planning Overhaul keeps seventy thousand little decisions from becoming your new full-time job.

[b]Plan every layer. Move what matters. Build the ship you actually drew.[/b]
